causes.text: T-Mobile's Q2 2023 earnings report showed industry-leading growth, with 299 thousand postpaid net account additions, 1.6 million postpaid net customer additions and high-speed internet net adds greater than AT&T, Verizon, Comcast and Charter combined for the fifth consecutive quarter.

source_info.title: T-Mobile reports Q2 2023 results with industry-leading growth

effects.text: On 22 February 2024, a prolonged nationwide network outage left tens of thousands of AT&T customers without service for nearly 12 hours; the outage highlighted fragility in telecom networks and caused AT&T stock to fall 2.4% as news spread.

source_info.title: AT&T network outage hits customers nationwide

causal_reasoning_chain.description: T-Mobile Q2 2023 results showed the company was attracting customers at a record pace. It added 1.6 million postpaid customers, with high-speed internet net adds more than AT&T and other competitors combined.
This created a perception that T-Mobile's network reliability and service had become a market benchmark, raising expectations for others in the telecom sector.
When AT&T suffered a nationwide outage in February 2024, the contrast with T-Mobile performance increased investor disappointment, leading to a 2.4% drop in AT&T's stock price.

rationale: T-Mobile strong performance raised the bar for telecom service reliability. AT&T's subsequent failure was judged more harshly in comparison, leading to a tangible financial impact.
counterfactual_analysis: Had T-Mobile not demonstrated such strong growth, AT&T outage might have been seen as an industry-wide risk, and investor response could have been milder.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Broad economic factors on the day of the outage might have contributed to the stock drop independently of T-Mobile's success.

details.commentary: AT&T's decision to outsource part of its 5G build to Ericsson underscored how intense the competition for scale and efficiency had become in telecom equipment. The move validated Ericsson's technology and positioned it more strongly against rivals in winning large, multi-year radio contracts.

As more operators commit to Ericsson's 5G platforms, the company gains learning-curve benefits and a larger installed base to monetize with software and services. Those scale advantages can, in turn, help it win future tenders, creating a reinforcing loop between contract wins, performance and investor confidence.
